summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with chronic pancreatitis, depression, and a history of C. difficile infection, was admitted with nausea, vomiting, and severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back. She was found to have a recurrence of Clostridium difficile colitis, confirmed by a positive stool PCR test. She was treated with IV metronidazole and oral vancomycin, along with IV fluids and her established pain and nausea protocol including Dilaudid, promethazine, and lorazepam. A right PICC line was placed for reliable access. Her symptoms improved, she transitioned to oral intake, and her labs stabilized. Blood pressure was managed with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. She was discharged home on a full course of vancomycin, with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and continue all home medications including Creon, amitriptyline, and quetiapine.
